set.approach: From the top of the Needles gondola at Snowbasin, follow the road that runs over the Middle Bowl lift, then the trail heading for Middle Bowl Cirque. Where the trail starts to climb, cut left and scramble loose talus to the foot of the Lone Tree chute, then go left to the wall forming its east side. Scramble up to the obvious dihedral, which is visible from the gondola.
set.descent_text: Two ways down. Walk off east into the east chute beside Lone Tree and scramble down its scree and dirt, which can involve some bushwhacking to reach the chute. Or rappel from the belay tree at the top of the route; a long rope makes this straightforward, and a shorter rope would need some creativity.

review.notes: Route page gives the base location from the gondola side and two ways down; area page gives the gondola start.

set.approach: Start from the top of the Needles gondola at Snowbasin and climb the west-side chute through the Lone Tree ski run, going past the On the Fly slab. Just before the shallow dihedral, a set of cracks splits a face on the left-hand side of On the Fly, and that is the line.

review.notes: Route page places the crack relative to On the Fly in the west Lone Tree chute; area page gives the gondola approach. No descent stated, so none written.

set.approach: Head for the steep flank over the Strawberry Traverse, under the pale gray north-face slab that holds the start of On the Fly. Turn the corner just right of the huge solitary tree; the base is in a shaded alcove above a large healthy tree, facing the Needles Lodge.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the top of the peak. Walk off from the summit.

review.notes: Route page: one long pitch to the top of the peak, then a walk off; base placed by the north face slab and the big tree.

set.approach: From the top of the Needles gondola take the road toward the Middle Bowl lift, continuing as though heading for the DeMoisy chairlift. After the road drops down a steep hill the face comes into view; scramble up to its base.
set.descent_text: The route ends at a large tree above the third pitch. From there, walk off.

review.notes: Route page: base reached by road from the gondola; top belay at a large tree then walk off.

set.descent_text: After the second pitch, a short stretch of broken third-class ground leads to the summit ridge. Parties can walk west off the top, or rappel the line.

review.notes: Route page: after the second pitch, a short stretch of third class reaches the summit ridge; walk off west or rappel.

set.approach: Reach the South Summit Wall directly from the meadow by crossing the talus field. The route begins to the right of the buttress that holds Center Thumb, as seen from below, and moves toward the middle of the formation.

review.notes: Route page places it right of the Center Thumb formation; area page gives the meadow and talus access. No descent written.

set.approach: Reach the South Summit Wall directly from the meadow by crossing the talus field. The route follows the first corner system to the left of Taivallista.

review.notes: Route page: first corner system left of Taivallista; area page: access across meadow talus. No descent written.

set.approach: Hike south on the most-used trail along the east side of Hopkins Lake. About halfway along the lake, look up and to the left, roughly 50 yards off the trail, for the slabs that hold the route.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the large tree at the belay ledge above the crux crack. Two climbers can rappel at once, and the rope pulls without trouble.

review.notes: Route page: slab crack above Hopkins Lake, rappel from a large tree.

mt_leggat_spire_bootleggar.skip_reason: Route page defers its approach and descent to other routes' pages; not enough about this line alone

set.approach: Reach the base of the north face first by the long approach in from the Benbow Mine side. From a camp there, hike up the fresh, light-colored moraine toward the southeast to a bowl under the big east-summit face, then wrap around to the east side of the Central Rib. Start scrambling where dark rock shows at the toe of the rib.
set.descent_text: From the west summit, drop back to the big ledge and traverse over to the east summit, which is third class with easy routefinding. Descend east, then north to northeast, onto the Mt. Wood plateau, and continue down scree and talus toward the base of the north face, keeping the distinct darker slope on the left to avoid cliffs. Rejoin the moraine and retrace the approach to camp.

review.notes: Route page gives the final approach and a full descent; the long approach is by reference to the parent North Face page.

set.approach: Follow the Lake Fork trail toward Black Canyon Lake and turn off at the stock bridge, near the fifth mile. A use trail leads from there to the base of the north face, a wall of roughly 1,200 feet.

review.notes: Area page gives the turn-off and use trail. No descent source, none written.

mt_reynolds_mountain_southwestern_talus_.skip_reason: Name and grade (5.9+ on a talus slope) look like a hiking route misfiled as trad; no source searched or found, identity unconfirmed

set.approach: From the Fairy Lake trailhead, head for Sacajawea Peak. In the bowl between Hardscrabble Peak and Sacajawea, find the obvious slab at the foot of the peak, which is the start.
set.descent_text: Above the climbing, continue along the ridge between the Airplane bowl and the Sacajawea bowl to the summit, then walk down the regular hiking trail.

review.notes: Route and area pages agree on the slab start and the descent by the regular trail.

set.approach: Follow the Spirit Mountain approach to Moon Lake. From the south end of the lake, skirt the east shore and aim for the snow at the foot of the arete, then climb the steep permanent snowfield, which steepens to about 50 degrees near its top, to the base of the rock.
set.descent_text: Descend by the South Ridge, which is longer than the alternative. The South Slopes route is shorter but can hold alpine ice in the snowfield and has very loose fourth-class terrain beside it.

review.notes: Route page: approach from Moon Lake to the base, two descent options.

set.approach: Park at the East Rosebud Creek bridge below the towers, then scramble the steep gully that separates Innocence from Incubus. Start from a ledge beneath two opposing dihedrals at the bottom of Incubus. The lower tier can be bypassed by continuing up the gully to the big midway terrace.
set.descent_text: A bolted rappel station sits roughly 30 feet below the summit, reached from a tree. Long rappels from there reach the big midway ledge, and from that terrace you walk off.

review.notes: Route and area pages: gully between Innocence and Incubus; bolted rappel station below the summit, walk off the midway terrace.

set.approach: Take the Hoffer Lakes trail beyond the lakes until a climbers trail branches off and leads to the base of the wall near Lee's Peak.
set.descent_text: Rather than climbing the optional last pitch to the walk-off, rappel the route to the tree by the first-pitch anchor, because the rock above is chossy. A long rope is needed.

review.notes: Route page: Hoffer Lakes trail then climbers trail; rappel preferred to topping out.

set.approach: From the Howlock Mountain trailhead at the north end of Diamond Lake, take the Howlock Mountain trail to a junction and turn right onto the Thielsen Creek trail. At its junction with the Pacific Crest Trail, continue straight up the Thielsen Creek drainage toward the remnants of the old glacier. The route starts on the east side of the former glacier at the foot of the northeast buttress, with easy slabs below a system of right-facing dihedrals.
set.descent_text: Finish by scrambling the summit block by its regular south line, then descend the West Ridge. Getting back depends on whether a car or bikes were left at the Mt. Thielsen trailhead or the party walked in from Diamond Lake.

review.notes: Route page gives approach via Howlock Mountain trail and the Thielsen Creek drainage, and the summit-block and West Ridge descent.

set.approach: Take the Mount Thielsen trail from the trailhead to the Pacific Crest Trail junction, then follow the well-used climbers path up toward the summit horn. Where the fourth-class trail nears the summit pinnacle, bear left rather than right and walk clockwise around the base of the pinnacle until the ledge ends at a cliff. A small to medium ledge there serves as the belay stance at the start of the arete.

review.notes: Route page gives the base; trail to the horn from the hiking guide.

az_bushmaster_peak_lachesis_thread_of_li.skip_reason: No source found for this route; identity unconfirmed

set.approach: The ridge starts at the second Sandia tram tower. Reach it by the West Ridge trail, or by Domingo Baca Canyon, which is also the better way to the east side of the peak.
set.descent_text: From the summit, contour the slopes north of Whiskey Peak, dropping gradually to about 9,400 feet into the top of the forested gully just west of the Thumb. That gully leads down to the Old La Luz trail.

review.notes: Route and area pages: ridge begins at the second tram tower; descent contours north slopes to the gully west of the Thumb.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route from its bolted anchors with two ropes. The route stops below the top of the cliff, so there is no walk-off.

review.notes: Route page: bolted rappel anchors, rappel the route.

ny_lookout_mountain_anabasis.skip_reason: Crag route; one-pitch offwidth ending at the top of a cliff, descent is not a peak descent

set.approach: From the Hautes-Gorges park gate, take the shuttle or ride a bike to the Draveur visitor centre. Cross the bridge over the dam on foot, turn left on a hiking trail and follow it a few minutes. When a small island appears in the Malbaie River, cut straight into the woods toward the gully and climb the talus to the foot of the large friction slab.
set.descent_text: Descend by rappelling from trees to the right of the route. A short optional hike leads to the trailless summit of the mountain.

review.notes: Route page: approach from the Draveur visitor centre; descent by rappel from trees at the right.

qc_mount_f_lix_antoine_savard_le_chemin_.skip_reason: Its only page gives no approach, descent or location; nothing to write

set.approach: From Fairy Meadows, skirt the left flank of East Huey Spire and head straight up the grassy slope once there is a way past the tower, avoiding excess talus hopping. The snow-filled gully on the southwest side is the start; follow it, or the moss slabs to its left, up to the saddle that lies between East Huey and Middle Huey. Consider roping up for this section when the moss is damp or ice lingers in the gully.
set.descent_text: Descend the route by rappelling. Fixed rappel stations in the gully help.

review.notes: Route page: approach around the left of the spire to a gully and notch; descend the route.

nt_east_huey_spire_riders_on_the_storm.skip_reason: Grade does not match: the only page found gives a higher overall grade than the row (5.12b); identity unconfirmed

set.approach: Starting at Fairy Meadows, hike to the foot of the tower; a snowfield lies on the way. Its first pitch begins roughly 100 feet to the right of the starting chimney of the Southeast Face.

review.notes: Route page: starts about 100 ft right of the SE Face; area page: approach from Fairy Meadows.

set.descent_text: Descent is long and serious. From the summit follow the third- and fourth-class west ridge down to the low point just before Parrot Beak Peak. From there, follow a steep, loose sandy goat trail down the gullies, downclimbing slabs and fourth-class grassy ledges, back into the main drainage below Lotus Flower Tower.

review.notes: Route page gives the descent in detail; no approach text.

set.approach: From Fairy Meadows, use the sparsely cairned path along the right edge of the meadow, then go up the southern drainage (the other fork goes to Lotus Flower Tower) to the foot of the Terrace Tower wall.

review.notes: Route and area pages: Fairy Meadows trail and southern drainage. No descent source.

set.approach: Go up the drainage south of Fairy Meadows (the north fork heads to Lotus Flower Tower) to the foot of the wall on Terrace Tower. The route climbs the right side of the white pillar on the east face, starting as The White Tower does.
set.descent_text: Descend by rappelling the neighboring White Tower line, whose top sits some 30 feet to the left. Use two ropes.

review.notes: Route page: start as for The White Tower; descent by rappelling that route. Area page: approach.

set.approach: Go up the drainage south of Fairy Meadows (the north fork heads to Lotus Flower Tower) to the foot of the wall on Terrace Tower. The line follows the left edge of the conspicuous white pillar that fills the east face.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route using two ropes, backing up the rappel stations with extra webbing.

review.notes: Route page: left side of the white pillar, rappel with two ropes. Area page: approach.

set.approach: Walk up the little creek below the face, aiming for the highest tower. The first, lowest peak to the right carries Kusawa Stairs in its center.

review.notes: Route page gives the location.

set.approach: Start about 300 meters left of Kusawa Stairs, on a small slab to the left of a big dihedral that divides the face.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route.

review.notes: Route page gives location and descent.

yt_ark_mountain_east_face_the_king.skip_reason: Its page says it has no information and the grade is unknown; identity unconfirmed

set.approach: Park at the pullout overlooking Choutla Lake and hike toward the base of the lowest talus, following it up along the right-hand side of the big gully that drains most of the south face. Do not go straight up the gully, which is exposed to overhead rockfall. Sidehill on third-class ground to a tree weakness over a rib, descend the backside to the base of the ribbed south face, then aim right up slabs and talus to the rib where red loose rock meets solid black rock.
set.descent_text: Walk down to skier's left of the face and return to the parking pullout.

review.notes: Route page gives approach and descent.

set.approach: Park at the small pullout by the Choutla Lake sign, off the Tagish road east of Carcross, and bushwhack toward the obvious large gully. Cross the gully early rather than late, and aim for a rocky knoll before the main ridge. Past the knoll, a talus gully lies between two rocky ridges; the route follows the left-hand ridge, which has a light-colored granite bump and sits right beside the very large south-face gully.
set.descent_text: From the summit, contour the back side of the peak toward Carcross to an obvious split in the ridgeline. Go south through the talus-filled split to a vegetated slope, follow the spur on the left rather than the gully on the right, and continue to a willow patch. From there a long, steep bushwhack returns to the road.

review.notes: Route page gives the approach and a descent line; area page gives the pullout.

yt_glave_peak_three_guardsmen_nw_ridge.skip_reason: Only page says the grade is unknown and describes a first ascent of other summits; identity unconfirmed

yt_matheson_ridge_matheson_peak.skip_reason: the only page is an ungraded ridge traverse; identity unconfirmed

set.approach: The route is on the unnamed sub-peak just north of Mt. Kelsall. From camp, traverse beneath the north face of Mt. Kelsall over talus and scree to a cliff band in the middle of the valley. Take the right-hand exit, cross a short glacier, then go north to the base of the climb.
set.descent_text: Walk off the summit to the northwest.

review.notes: Route page gives approach from camp and the walk off.

set.approach: There is no trail. Start by bushwhacking through thick alder in the ditch, then pick a line through alpine meadows and rock slabs among krummholz and juniper toward the obvious slab. The route starts at the left end of the slab, where the first pitch's bolt line is visible.
set.descent_text: Walk off by contouring left to an obvious gully and following it to the base of the slab; the gully has slippery heather and some exposed slab. Or rappel the line as pitched.

review.notes: Route page: walk-off and rappel options. Area page: no-trail approach.
